:::{#exr-mle-use-log}
#### Comparing likelihoods through log-likelihoods

Suppose $\Lik(\th) > 0$ for every $\th$.
Show that a parameter value $\th^*$ maximizes the likelihood $\Lik$
if and only if it maximizes the [log-likelihood](#def-loglik) $\lik$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-mle-use-log}

The natural logarithm is strictly increasing on $(0, \infty)$,
so for any $\th_1$ and $\th_2$,
$\Lik(\th_1) \ge \Lik(\th_2)$ if and only if $\log \Lik(\th_1) \ge \log \Lik(\th_2)$,
that is, $\lik(\th_1) \ge \lik(\th_2)$.
So $\th^*$ satisfies $\Lik(\th^*) \ge \Lik(\th)$ for every $\th$
if and only if it satisfies $\lik(\th^*) \ge \lik(\th)$ for every $\th$.

:::
